title: Endurance Profile
conditions: Basic fuel 84 US gal, weight 3600 lb at start, gear and flaps retracted, mixture best economy cruise. No allowance for wind beyond the 45-minute reserve already baked into the chart.

verification.note: Re-measured pixel-by-pixel against reference/fig5-14-endurance-profile.png on 2026-10-01 (BASIC FUEL 84 gal solid curves only). The original at16000 values (all exactly +1.0 hr above seaLevel for every curve) look like an assumed uniform rise rather than a measured one -- the real per-curve rises are much smaller and uneven (0.25 to 0.5 hr), and like fig 5-12/5-13, not every curve reaches 16000 ft.

75.note: Clean sharp termination at 8000 ft, unambiguous.

65.note: Clean sharp termination at 12000 ft, unambiguous.

55.note: Terminates close to but not exactly at 16000 ft.

45.note: LOWER CONFIDENCE: this curve runs close beside the 55% curve and briefly overlaps/crosses it near the top of the chart, which made the two hard to separate pixel-by-pixel. The seaLevel value (5.85) is solid, but the top-end value is a best estimate, not a clean independent read. Worth a second look with a higher-res source scan if this number matters.

verification.correctionVsOriginal: seaLevel values were already close to accurate in the original (45: 5.8 vs 5.85, 55: 5.0 vs 5.14, 65: 4.5 vs 4.56, 75: 4.0 vs 4.0 exactly). The at16000 values were the main correction -- the original's uniform +1.0 hr assumption overstated every curve's altitude benefit, especially 75% (claimed 5.0, real extrapolated value ~4.5) and 65% (claimed 5.5, real ~4.7).

confidence.45: medium - seaLevel point solid, ceiling point approximate (see realCeilings note)
